```{r restrict_dates2019}
# create inflation column, make quarterly, and limit 1960-2019
cpi19 <- cpi_full |>
  dplyr::filter(observation_date >= as.Date("1959-12-01")) |>
  dplyr::filter(lubridate::month(observation_date) %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(quarter = tsibble::yearquarter(observation_date)) |>
  tsibble::as_tsibble(index=quarter) |>
  dplyr::mutate(inflation = 400 * log(CPIAUCSL / dplyr::lag(CPIAUCSL))) |>
  dplyr::filter(quarter >= tsibble::yearquarter("1960 Q1")) |> 
  dplyr::filter(quarter <= tsibble::yearquarter("2019 Q4")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(d_inflation = inflation - lag(inflation, 1))

# make quarterly and limit 1960-2019
unemp19 <- unemp_full |>
  dplyr::filter(observation_date >= as.Date("1960-01-01")) |>
  dplyr::filter(lubridate::month(observation_date) %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(quarter = tsibble::yearquarter(observation_date)) |>
  tsibble::as_tsibble(index=quarter) |> 
  dplyr::filter(quarter <= tsibble::yearquarter("2019 Q4")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(d_unrate = UNRATE - lag(UNRATE, 1))

summary(cpi19)
summary(unemp19)
```

# 4.4. Step 3: Implement the core forecasting models

```{r models}
### Model 1: random walk



### Model 2: 4-quarter-average benchmarks



### Model 3: AR(p) model: AR(3) selected
forecast_ar <- function(x, h = 8) {
  # estimate AR(1) through AR(4)
  models <- lapply(1:4, function(p) {
    arima(x, order = c(p, 0, 0), method = "ML")
  })
  # select the model with the lowest BIC
  bic <- sapply(models, bic)
  best_model <- models[[which.min(bic)]]
  # forecast the next h quarters
  predict(best_model, n.ahead = h)$pred
}


### Model 4: direct AR 



### Construct the local mean using simple exponential smoothing (this is needed in fixed-persistence model)
# FROM ARIEL
# 4.4.5 Local mean by simple exponential smoothing --------------------------
# tau_1960Q1 = pi_1960Q1, tau_t = (1 - alpha) * tau_{t-1} + alpha * pi_t,
# with alpha = 0.05 fixed by the project (not estimated).
local_mean <- function(pi, alpha = 0.05) {
  stopifnot(length(pi) > 0, !anyNA(pi))
  tau <- numeric(length(pi))
  tau[1] <- pi[1]
  for (t in seq_along(pi)[-1]) {
    tau[t] <- (1 - alpha) * tau[t - 1] + alpha * pi[t]
  }
  tau
}

# Adds `tau` (local mean) and `gap` (pi_t - tau_t) to a sample.
# Call it on the origin-T sample, which must start in 1960Q1 so tau is
# initialized at pi_1960Q1. The last row then holds tau_T and g_T.
#   Gap AR (4.4.6):          fit the AR to data$gap, forecast = tau_T + g-hat
#   Fixed persistence (4.4.7): forecast = tau_T + 0.46^h * g_T
add_local_mean <- function(data, alpha = 0.05) {
  data$tau <- local_mean(data$Inflation, alpha)
  data$gap <- data$Inflation - data$tau
  data
}



### Model 5: gap AR model



### Model 6: Fixed persistence gap forecast 
forecast_fixed_gap <- function(local_mean, gap, h=8, rho = 0.46) {
  tau_T <- tail(local_mean, 1)
  gap_T <- tail(gap, 1)
  
  forecast <- tau_T + rho^seq_len(h) * gap_T
  
  return(forecast)
}

# Model 7: direct Phillips-curve model
```

```{r exp_window}

inflation_quarters <- cpi19$quarter

n_total <- length(inflation_values)

# identify forecast origin and end
first_origin_index <- which(
  inflation_quarters == tsibble::yearquarter("1999 Q4")
)
last_origin_index <- which(
  inflation_quarters == tsibble::yearquarter("2019 Q3")
)

forecast_rows <- list()
row_id <- 1

for (origin_index in first_origin_index:last_origin_index) {
  # use only observations through origin T
  train_index <- seq_len(origin_index)
  train_values <- inflation_values[train_index]
  
  # =======
  # Models
  # =======
  # Model 1: random walk without drift
  
  # Model 2: 4-quarter-average benchmark
  
  # Model 3: AR(p) --> AR(3)
  ar_forecasts <- forecast_arp(train_values, h = 8) 
  # Model 4: direct AR
  
  # construct local mean and inflation gap (Ariel's code above)
  train_data <- tibble::tibble(
    Inflation = train_values
  )
  train_data <- add_local_mean(train_data, alpha = 0.05)
  local_mean_history <- train_data$tau
  gap_history <- train_data$gap
  # Model 5: gap AR model
  
  # Model 6: fixed persistence gap forecast
  fixed_gap_forecasts <- forecast_fixed_gap(
    local_mean = local_mean_history,
    gap = gap_history,
    h = 8,
    rho = 0.46
  )

}
```

# Step 4: Evaluate the forecasts

```{r}
# calculate forecast accuracy by model and horizon
accuracy_results <- forecast_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(Model, h) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_h = dplyr::n(),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(Error^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(Error)),
    Mean_error = mean(Error), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(h) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Relative_RMSE = RMSE / RMSE[Model == "Four-quarter average"]
    ) |>
      dplyr::ungroup() |>
      dplyr::arrange(h, RMSE)

accuracy_table <- accuracy_results |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Model,
    Horizon = h,
    n_h,
    RMSE,
    `Relative RMSE` = Relative_RMSE,
    MAE,
    `Mean error` = Mean_error
  )

knitr::kable(
  accuracy_table,
  digits = 3,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "Expanding-window forecast accuracy"
)
```

## Step 5: Diagnose the leading one-step model (fixed-persistence gap forecast, I believe)

```{r selected_model_lag_gap}

# refit data through 2019Q4
inflation19 <- cpi19$inflation

# construct local mean and inflation gap
local_mean19 <- construct_local_mean(
  inflation19, alpha = 0.05
)
gap19 <- inflation19 - local_mean19

# fixed persistence coefficient
rho <- 0.46

# generate one step fitted predictions for fixed persistence gap forecast
fixed_fitted <- c(
  NA_real_,
  head(local_mean19, -1) + rho * head(gap19,-1)
)
# calculate one-step prediction errors
fixed_residuals <- inflation19 - fixed_fitted

# create residuals
residual_data <- tibble::tibble(
  quarter = cpi19$quarter,
  residual = fixed_residuals
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(residual))

# residual time plot plus ACF/PACF
residual_data |>
  tsibble::as_tsibble(index = quarter) |>
  feasts::gg_tsdisplay(residual, plot_type="partial", lag_max = 20)
```

```{r ljung_box}
lb_result <- stats::Box.test(
  residual_data$residual,
  lag = 12,
  type = "Ljung-Box",
  fitdf = 0
)
lb_result
```


```{r res_variability}
# residual variability
residual_data <- residual_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rolling_sd = slider::slide_dbl(
      residual,
      sd,
      .before = 19,
      .complete = TRUE
    )
  )

residual_data |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(x=quarter, y = rolling_sd)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() + 
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Fixed-persistence gap model: residual variability",
    x = "Quarter",
    y = "20-quarter rolling standard deviation"
  ) + 
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```


```{r resid_summary}
# numerical residual summary
tibble::tibble(
  Mean = mean(gap_residuals),
  SD = sd(gap_residuals),
  Minimum = min(gap_residuals),
  Maximum = max(gap_residuals),
  RMSE = sqrt(mean(gap_residuals^2))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
